chunk_map.heading: H1/lede — Fork the worktree, carry the evidence

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No chunk points at another file by position; the only source pointer is the module's own framing (established via include-order carve-out, rule 1), not a positional cross-file callback.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw' backward-beat construction anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction in this file; it is a straight fork-and-verify exercise, not a demo beat.

Every chunk carries a self-standing claim or instruction (chunk 0 frames the split-test point; chunk 1 gives the fork prompt; chunk 2 gives the verification check; chunk 3 gives the recovery ladder) — none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Harm this rule prevents: a projected header sets the room's expectation for the whole slide, and a reader can't glance elsewhere to reconcile a contradiction. Harm is present: chunk 3's header 'If the coordinates are missing' is immediately followed by a bullet describing the SUCCESS path — 'Claude reads the protected Run coordinates block in task.md, uses the m4/<slug> branch named there, and forks from that branch's "M4 starting point" commit' (line 36) — which is the exact same action Phase 1's prompt already performs when the block IS present, not what to do when it's missing. Traced via git history: the pre-extraction section was neutrally titled '## Anchor the fork to the run coordinates' (git show 119236f^:.../learn-from-the-test.md) and covered normal-path + two fallbacks under that neutral title; today's extraction renamed the header to the 'If…missing' framing but kept bullet 1 verbatim, so the header now promises a scenario the first bullet doesn't describe.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Retitle the header to something neutral like 'Anchor the fork to the run coordinates' (matching the pre-extraction title), or move bullet 1 out and let the header govern only the two genuine fallback bullets.

rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction, no anaphora/epistrophe triples, no self-grading superlatives, no number-with-retraction, no abstraction-noun stacks, no empty-leg verb triplets in any chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No repo/maintainer vocabulary (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) appears in any chunk; language stays in engineer register (worktree, branch, commit, coordinates).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0's bold labels (Time, Session, What you do, What you build, The point) are the standing exercise-metadata template used across the exercise library (e.g. curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md carries the identical Time/Session/What you do/What you build/The point pattern) — established handle convention, not narrative bold. No other bold appears in chunks 1-3 beyond the widget's own 'Prompt' chrome label.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: File is included into the module body as an [Exercise: …] link, which the module renderer wraps in a .phase--exercise wrapper reaching the composed deck; no phase-less prose section at risk here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only one 'Phase 1' header exists in this file (no hand-numbered Phase 2+ to go out of sequence), and no in-file 'Step K'/'Phase K' cross-reference points elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'below/above/further down/at the top of this page' positional pointers anywhere in the body; chunk 2's 'the two paths Claude checked' resolves within the same chunk (CLAUDE.local.md and observations/ are both named in that chunk's own first sentence).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No in-body links in this file at all (the file itself is the target of an include-link elsewhere, not a source of one).
